00 · Start here
A growth breakdown for Photoroom
Why we made this

On 29 October you launched Video Ad Maker, a few weeks after a16z named Photoroom one of only seven companies on all three of its Top 100 lists: web, mobile and consumer spending. Your app already exports photos sized for Etsy, Depop, Poshmark and Vinted, and Depop built your tools straight into its listing flow.

The moment that sells Photoroom is visual: a crumpled top on a bedroom floor becomes a clean listing photo in seconds. This board is how we would put that moment in front of resellers every day, through the busiest selling weeks of the year. It is free, so take whatever is useful.

How to read this board
Use the list on the left, or press P to go frame by frame. On a phone, just scroll.
Creator cards: platform, followers and median views on recent videos.
Please note
Made by hypjam from public information, checked 30 Oct 2026. Nobody at Photoroom asked for this, and it is not paid work. The creators named here have not been contacted and have no link to hypjam: they show the kind of people we would cast.
12 resellers and shop owners shortlisted, 4 scripts with 32 hooks, and a first month built around the floor-to-listing moment, from Black Friday to January clear-outs.
Four numbers to remember
300M+: Photoroom users, from your App Store page
7 billion: images made with Photoroom every year, from your about page
1 of 7: companies on all three a16z Top 100 lists: web, mobile and spending (5 Oct)
53%: of Americans have sold or expect to sell things they own to help pay for the holidays (ThredUp, 26 Oct)
Who made this

hypjam is a UGC agency in London. We cast, script, direct and edit creators for consumer startups, and run the best videos as ads.

01 · Why UGC
Why creator videos work
Authenticity
People trust people
"Remove any background" is a claim. A reseller holding up the real top, then showing the listing photo it became, is proof.
Show, do not tell
The before and after is the ad
A crumpled shirt on the floor, then a clean listing photo seconds later. Nobody needs the feature explained once they have seen it.
Objections
Answer "is that the real item?" on camera
Resale buyers buy the exact piece in the photo. A creator who holds the real item next to the finished photo answers that before anyone asks.
A real moment
The busiest selling weeks of the year
Black Friday is 27 November, and more than half of Americans have sold or expect to sell things to pay for the holidays. Videos now meet people while their closets are coming out.
Fuel for ads
Your best ads come from creators
The strongest creator videos run as TikTok Spark Ads and Meta partnership ads, with 8 openings per script, so the budget follows what people actually watch.
Doesn't feel like an ad
Looks like a normal reseller post
So people actually watch it instead of scrolling past. It is still labelled as an ad, it just does not feel like one.
02 · What we learned
Where Photoroom is today
The product
Remove and replace backgrounds, add AI shadows, smooth creases with Unwrinkle, make ghost mannequins, flat lays and AI fashion model shots, batch edit hundreds of photos at once, and export sized for Shopify, Amazon, Etsy, Depop, Poshmark and Vinted. Now video too: product videos, and Video Ad Maker for Meta, TikTok and YouTube. On iPhone, Android and the web.
The scale
300M+ users, and 4.8 stars from 231K ratings on the US App Store. 7 billion images a year and 1M+ businesses, from your about page. One of seven companies on all three of a16z's Top 100 lists (5 October). Backed by Y Combinator, S20.
Built into marketplaces
Depop put your background removal, AI shadows and resizing inside its listing flow: 1M+ listings so far. Mercari added your background blur to its camera. Vestiaire Collective now runs its new listing photos through Photoroom, and in its test those listings sold at a 5% higher rate.
Already in motion
  • Video Ad Maker, launched on 29 October: product photos in, a video ad with actors, music and voiceover out.
  • A TikTok account with 799.8K followers, where "Meet the Photoroom team" has 32.4M plays.
  • An affiliate program on Awin for creators and sellers, and reseller customer stories, like Alex Mahl's Poshmark shop and the vintage reseller Blonde Bandit.
What that tells us
Sellers already trust Photoroom at enormous scale, and marketplaces build it into their own apps. What is missing is volume: real resellers showing the floor-to-listing moment on TikTok and Reels every day, in their own words.
The timing
Black Friday is 27 November and Cyber Monday 30 November. 62% of Americans plan to buy secondhand this season (ThredUp, 26 October), and Video Ad Maker is new right when every small shop needs a holiday ad.
Sources: photoroom.com (home, about, company, Video Ad Maker, Unwrinkle, affiliates, the Depop, Mercari, Alex Mahl and Blonde Bandit stories, and the Vestiaire Collective news of 13 October), the US App Store, the YC company page, a16z (5 Oct 2026), ThredUp's 2026 Holiday Resale Report (26 Oct 2026), @Photoroom on X and @photoroom on TikTok, all read 30 Oct 2026.

04 · The objection
"Is that the real item?": the objection to win
In resale the buyer buys the exact piece in the photo. So every video shows the real item first, then the clean listing photo, side by side.
What you already promise
  • Product Fidelity: colour, shape, materials and texture kept in every AI image
  • Models built for e-commerce hold the real product, so what ships matches what arrives
  • Unwrinkle keeps fabric texture, seams and natural shading
What buyers say
87% of shoppers in your UK survey say product visuals are the most important factor in a purchase, and 63% say inconsistent images make a marketplace less trustworthy (State of GenAI in Marketplaces 2026).
What marketplaces found
At Vestiaire Collective, listings edited with Photoroom sold at a 5% higher rate and digital authentication was unaffected. Mercari chose your background blur because it keeps the real look of the product.
How we use it
Every script shows the real item on camera before the edit, and the finished photo next to it. Wear and flaws stay visible in at least one photo.
Your own rule
Your marketplace guide says it plainly: most platforms require a product image to represent the actual item being sold. Creators start from a real photo of the real item, every time.
What creators never say
No "nobody will notice", no hiding wear, no promises about sales or profits, and nothing your pages do not say Photoroom does.
05 · Audience
Who to sell to first
Start here
Clothing resellers on Depop, Poshmark, eBay and Vinted
They photograph clothes on beds, floors and chairs and list dozens a week. Background removal, Unwrinkle and Batch are their daily routine. Formats A and B.
Start here
People clearing out their closets
53% of Americans have sold or expect to sell things they own to help pay for the holidays. First-time sellers need one clean photo, fast. Format A.
Broadest reach
People who shop secondhand
62% of Americans plan to buy secondhand this season. A "would you buy it?" before and after pulls in buyers and sellers alike. Format C.
Next
Small shops and vintage booths
Etsy sellers, vintage racks and market vendors who need a Black Friday ad, not just a photo. Video Ad Maker turns their product photos into one. Format D.
Where we would start
Clothing resellers first: they list every day, the before and after is already their routine, and every video ends with something a viewer can copy with their own closet. Every creator we cast and every audience we target is an adult.
06 · The moment
From Black Friday to January clear-outs
Black Friday is 27 November and Cyber Monday 30 November, and more than half of Americans plan to sell things to pay for the holidays. Videos started now are tested by the peak and still working in January.
Now to 22 November
Resellers film Scripts A and B as they list their holiday stock. The first TikTok Spark Ads and Meta partnership ads go live, pointing at the App Store and Google Play.
Thanksgiving to Cyber Monday
Shop owners film Script D: a Black Friday ad made in Video Ad Maker from four product photos. Budget moves to the hooks that drive downloads.
December into January
Gift listings and last-minute sales, then January clear-outs: the batch videos keep running as ads while closets empty.
What this needs from you
  • A Photoroom account for each creator on the plan the scripts need, including Video Ad Maker
  • A tracking link per creator to the App Store, Google Play or the web app
  • One person on your team who signs off within 48 hours
Why not wait for January?
Videos filmed in early November are tested and cut by Black Friday, so the budget goes to proven hooks in the busiest weeks, and again when January clear-outs start.
07 · The first month
Your first four weeks
Week 1 · 9-15 Nov
You approve the shortlist and the 4 formats. We sign creators and send each a script with 8 hooks. Creators use Photoroom on their own listings for a few days before anyone films.
Week 2 · 16-22 Nov
First videos come in and we review each within 48 hours. Floor-to-listing and batch videos go first, cut into 15 and 30 second ads.
Week 3 · 23-29 Nov
Thanksgiving and Black Friday: shop owners post their Video Ad Maker videos, and budget moves to the openings and creators that drive downloads.
Week 4 · 30 Nov-6 Dec
Cyber Monday, then a results review together: downloads by creator and by ad, and the plan for December gifting and January clear-outs.
If it is a yes this week
Agreements signed and accounts set up by Friday. First videos live within 14 days of the scripts being signed off.

Takeaway
Resale videos break out when they show the real work: the lot, the day, the routine. So we would run many everyday sellers side by side, testing 8 hooks per script.
Where the market is
Resellers post hauls, routines and sales every day, and full-time sellers reach millions. The floor-to-listing moment is the one we would lead with, because it is the moment Photoroom owns.
10 · Script A
Script A: From the floor to the listing
The brief

Where: TikTok and Instagram Reels from the creator's account, plus TikTok Spark Ads and Meta partnership ads to the App Store and Google Play (15s and 30s cuts)

Length: 30-35s master. 30s cut: shots 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8. 15s cut: shots 1, 2, 5 and 8 (hook, disclosure, before and after, CTA).

Goal: Photoroom app downloads

Who films it: A US clothing reseller, 18+, who lists on Depop, Poshmark, eBay or Vinted and photographs at home. Filmed in their real room with a phone on a stand, plus a screen recording of Photoroom on their phone. The item is one they are really listing this week, photographed where it lies.

8 hooks to test (on screen, then spoken)
  1. This is how my listing photos really startThis is how every one of my listing photos actually starts.
  2. Crumpled on my floor. Listed in [time].This top is crumpled on my floor right now. Watch it get listed.
  3. I stopped ironing before I photographI don't iron anything before I photograph it anymore. Here's why.
  4. POV: you list from your bedroom floorIf you list from your bedroom floor, this one is for you.
  5. Same top. Same phone. [time] apart.Same top, same phone, about a minute apart.
  6. My [Depop] photos, before and afterThese are my [Depop] photos before, and these are after.
  7. No studio. No steamer. Just my phone.No studio, no steamer, just my phone and one app.
  8. Holiday clear-out: listing [number] things tonightI'm clearing out my closet for the holidays, starting with this one.

Product moment and call to action

Photoroom is named in the spoken disclosure at 0:02 and on screen from 0:09. Hero moment 0:09-0:20: the floor photo becomes the finished listing photo, shown next to the real top. That is the scene the 15s cut keeps.

CTA: Download Photoroom on the App Store or Google Play. In the ad cuts the button goes straight to the store page through the creator's tracking link.

Caption
Ad | Paid partnership with @photoroom. Floor to listing: [what you edited, one line, your words]. #ad #photoroom #reseller #depopseller #poshmarkseller
Rules for this video

FTC: 'Ad | Paid partnership with Photoroom' on screen from 0s to the end, a spoken disclosure by 0:05, the platform's paid partnership label switched on (TikTok, Instagram and YouTube), and the caption opens with the disclosure. Spark Ads and Meta partnership ads run from the creator's handle with Photoroom as the partner. Every item on camera is the creator's own and really for sale. The app is shown exactly as it works on the day on the creator's plan: nothing mocked up, re-rendered or edited outside Photoroom. The real item is shown next to the finished photo, and any wear, stain or flaw is photographed as it is. Each marketplace's own photo rules apply. No claims about sales, profits, prices or speed beyond what the creator really saw, and nothing photoroom.com does not say Photoroom does. Adults only (18+); no children on camera; no other people's names or addresses on screen (blur order slips and labels). Unwrinkle and the AI shadow are shown only as the app applies them; the creator never adds or removes details by hand.

Why it should convert
It shows the whole product in one before and after that anyone who has sold clothes recognises, and the real top held next to the finished photo answers the trust question before it is asked. A single transformation survives a 15s cut, which is what an app install ad needs.

13 · Script D
Script D: My Black Friday ad from four photos
The brief

Where: TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts from the shop owner's account, plus Meta partnership ads to the Video Ad Maker page

Length: 35-45s master. 30s cut: shots 1, 2, 4, 6 and 8.

Goal: Upgrades to the plans that include Video Ad Maker

Who films it: A US small shop owner, 18+: an Etsy seller, a vintage booth or a market vendor with a real product and a real holiday sale. Filmed at their work table or booth, with a screen recording of Video Ad Maker.

8 hooks to test (on screen, then spoken)

Rules for this video

FTC: 'Ad | Paid partnership with Photoroom' on screen from 0s to the end, a spoken disclosure by 0:05, the platform's paid partnership label switched on (TikTok, Instagram and YouTube), and the caption opens with the disclosure. Spark Ads and Meta partnership ads run from the creator's handle with Photoroom as the partner. Every item on camera is the creator's own and really for sale. The app is shown exactly as it works on the day on the creator's plan: nothing mocked up, re-rendered or edited outside Photoroom. The real item is shown next to the finished photo, and any wear, stain or flaw is photographed as it is. Each marketplace's own photo rules apply. No claims about sales, profits, prices or speed beyond what the creator really saw, and nothing photoroom.com does not say Photoroom does. Adults only (18+); no children on camera; no other people's names or addresses on screen (blur order slips and labels). If the finished ad uses an AI actor or an AI voice, the creator says so on camera and the ad carries each platform's AI-generated content label where the platform asks for it. Sale dates and offers are the shop's real ones.

Why it should convert
It is your newest launch, shown by the people it was built for, in the weeks every shop needs a holiday ad. A shop owner holding the real product next to the finished ad shows the product stays true, and small shops are the people most likely to upgrade for it.

16 · Ads
How the paid ads would run
1 · Film
Each script is shot once, with 8 different openings.
→
2 · Launch
Each opening runs as its own ad, from the creator's handle as a partnership ad.
→
3 · Read
After a few days we compare cost per download and how many people watch past 3 seconds.
4 · Cut
The weakest openings switch off and the budget moves to the best two.
→
5 · Remix
Winning hooks get new bodies and new creators.
→
6 · Refresh
New creator videos every week, so the ads never go stale.
Where the ads point
The App Store and Google Play, with one tracking link per creator, so every download traces back to the video that drove it. The same videos run as TikTok Spark Ads and Meta partnership ads, shown to adult resellers, thrifters and small shop owners.
Why partnership ads
Ads that run from a creator's own handle look like that creator's post, not a brand ad. That is the format these videos are built for.
What we would need
Each creator's OK for partnership ads, access to your TikTok and Meta ad accounts (or ad sets we run alongside your team), and a weekly look at downloads and upgrades.
17 · Process
How a campaign runs, step by step
1 · Brief
You tell us the goal, the audience and what can and can't be said about Photoroom.
→
2 · Cast
We shortlist creators by niche, location and median views. You pick.
→
3 · Offer
We send each creator the brief, the dates and the rate.
4 · Sign
A written agreement with every creator, covering usage and disclosure.
→
5 · Scripts
One per format: 8 hooks, a shot list, screens to record and a caption.
→
6 · Film and upload
Creators film on their phones and upload to a private folder only we see.
7 · Review
We check every video within 48 hours. Nothing posts unapproved.
→
8 · Post
On the creator's own account, with the ad disclosure and the paid-partnership label.
→
9 · Pay and report
Creators paid within 7 days of going live. You get a report every Monday.
Where creators talk to us
One hypjam Discord for every creator. Each campaign gets a private channel group for chat, scripts and posted links that only its creators and your team can see.
Accounts
Each signed creator gets a Photoroom account from you on the plan the scripts need, and uses it on their own listings for a few days before filming. Every item on camera is the creator's own.
18 · Reporting
What we report, and when
Every video
Views, how many people stay past 3 seconds, average watch time, saves, shares and comments.
Every creator link
A tracking link for each creator, so downloads trace back to the video that drove them.
Every Monday
A short report: every video, the hooks that won, downloads by creator, and what we change next.
Every month
A review call: spend, downloads, cost per result on anything run as an ad, and the plan for next month.
19 · Rules
Rules we never break
Disclosure
"Ad | Paid partnership with Photoroom" on screen, said in the first seconds, and the platform's paid-partnership label on. That is what the FTC asks for.
Who films
Adults only (18+). Creators use Photoroom themselves before they talk about it.
What gets said
Nothing your own pages do not say Photoroom does. No invented numbers. We never pay for a positive opinion, only for the video.
The real item, always
Every video starts from a real photo of the real item, and the finished photo is shown next to it. Wear and flaws stay visible, and each marketplace's own photo rules are followed.
No sales promises
Nobody says a photo sold an item or names a profit unless it is true for them. Creators speak for their own shop, never for a marketplace.
How we run it
Every video reviewed within 48 hours before it posts. Creators paid within 7 days of going live.
